seshat_added_entries.reason: Upstream's installer wrote the nine canonical speckit-* command skills but omitted the five speckit-git-* skills it emitted in the same commit (1eb0c98), leaving 5 of 14 vendored skills unverifiable on re-vendor. Closes KF-2 (docs/capabilities/ownership-audit.md section 5, finding 5), which spec 151 declared Out of Scope.
seshat_added_entries.hash_convention: sha256 over raw file bytes as checked out -- identical to the nine upstream-written entries here (verified reproducing before these were added). SCOPED TO THIS FILE: every entry is a .md pinned eol=lf by .gitattributes, so raw bytes and LF-normalized bytes coincide. The sibling speckit.manifest.json is NOT the same -- its five .ps1 entries verify only after normalizing CRLF to LF. Normalize before comparing there; see specs/151-speckit-fork-removal/research.md.
seshat_added_entries.on_revendor: Upstream will rewrite this file without these five entries and without this key. VERIFY (self-contained; run from the repo root, prints True per path): python -c "import json,hashlib,pathlib; m=json.load(open('.specify/integrations/claude.manifest.json')); [print(p, hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()==m['files'][p]) for p in m['seshat_added_entries']['paths']]". All five must print True: these have not changed upstream since 0.8.10, and the git blobs at 1eb0c98 are LF and hash to exactly these values. A False means upstream genuinely changed that file -- adopt the new bytes and update the hash rather than forcing the old one. TO RE-ADD after a re-vendor wipes them: restore this key and the five entries in `files` from git history (they were added in the KF-2 closure commit), then run the command above. If upstream begins pinning these five itself, delete this key and keep upstream's entries.
